judge_assessment.explanation: Every number the judge lists is correct and I recomputed all nine checks: 47-23 = 24, 68-35 = 33, the estimate 60-30 = 30 for 61-28, 52-27 = 25, 83-46 = 37, 90-50 = 40 alongside the exact 85-47 = 38, 74-58 = 16, and 63-29 = 34. The study guide's six checks are correct too (34, 45, 36, 27, and the estimate 20 for 54-27). But 'Independently checked all eight subtraction, estimation, regrouping, and error-analysis answers' overlooks what problem 8 actually asks. Its text is 'Explain what he should have done, then write the correct difference' -- two responses, of which verify.json covers one, the eval 63-29 = 34. There is no manual entry anywhere in this file, and final_response.md states '**Nothing on this sheet is left to manual review.**' That is a false claim of complete machine coverage on a sheet that asks a child to explain a regrouping error in writing; problem 6's 'say whether the exact answer is close to the estimate' is a second unflagged judgement. Coverage is also thinner than the count suggests elsewhere: problem 2 prints three responses ('Write how many ten rods and how many ones cubes are left, then write the number') against one entry (33), and problem 3 prints the two rounded numbers on lines plus the estimate ('__ - __') against one entry (30). The rod-and-cube counts and the rounded operands are the modelling steps this concept-models task exists to teach, and none of them is verified.

strengths_to_preserve: The sheet walks one subtraction method through four representations in a deliberate order -- cross out blocks (1), read the remaining rods and cubes as a number (2), estimate by rounding (3), expanded form with a broken ten (4, 5), and written subtraction against an error (8) -- so 'connect each model to mathematical notation' is realised as a sequence rather than a claim.

Problem 4 hands the student the first line of the work ('There are not enough ones to take 7 from 2, so break one ten: 52 = 40 + 12') and problem 5 withdraws exactly that scaffold for 83-46, which is the right way to fade support inside a guided-practice format.

Three declared misconception traps compute the wrong value from the wrong method (35, 43, 46 from taking the smaller ones digit from the larger), and the study guide's watch-out box states the rule that defeats all three: 'In 63 - 29 the ones column is 3 - 9, not 9 - 3. If the top digit is too small, break a ten -- do not swap.'

root_causes.description: Nothing forces an explanation prompt to carry a manual entry, so a worksheet can print 'Explain what he should have done' and still report zero manual items, and the delivery summary repeats that as complete coverage.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 8: 'Theo took the smaller ones digit away from the larger one instead of breaking a ten. Explain what he should have done, then write the correct difference.'
verify.json id 8 is a single eval entry (63-29 = 34); the file contains no manual entries at all.
final_response.md: '**Nothing on this sheet is left to manual review.**'
machine_observation records gate_chain_manual_flags: false, so the pipeline agreed.

root_causes.description: Coverage is per problem id rather than per printed response, so the intermediate place-value quantities the student is explicitly told to write are unchecked while only the final difference is verified.
evidence: Problem 2: 'Write how many ten rods and how many ones cubes are left, then write the number. 68 - 35 =' -> one entry, expected 33; the 3 rods and 3 cubes are unverified.
Problem 3: 'Round each number to the nearest ten and write the two rounded numbers on the lines. __ - __' -> one estimate entry, expected 30; the operands 60 and 30 are unverified.
Problem 6 asks for both an estimate and an exact answer and does carry two entries, showing the multi-entry pattern was available and simply not applied to 2 and 3.

improvements.title: Stop claiming zero manual review on a sheet whose problem 8 says 'Explain what he should have done'
improvements.proposed_change: Add a gate that scans each \problem body for explanation cues ('explain', 'tell how you know', 'say whether', 'why', 'describe') and fails the build unless that problem id also carries a manual entry. Derive the manual-review sentence in the delivery summary from verify.json rather than author prose, so 'Nothing on this sheet is left to manual review' cannot be printed while problems 6 and 8 ask for written judgement.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem text is 'Explain what he should have done, then write the correct difference' with a single eval entry: the gate must exit non-zero naming the id; the variant with an added manual entry must pass and report one manual item. Fails today -- curr-061 built green with exactly this shape.
improvements.expected_impact: Eliminates a false statement of complete verification in the delivered summary and attaches grading guidance to the explanation an adult actually has to read.
improvements.risk: Cue-word scanning will over-trigger on stems that merely narrate ('Theo took the smaller digit ...'); restrict matching to imperative sentences addressed to the student and allow an explicit author override.

improvements.title: Verify the rod-and-cube counts and the rounded operands, not only the final difference
improvements.proposed_change: Change the SKILL.md coverage rule from per-problem-id to per-rendered-answer-slot and enforce it in tests/check_layout.py by counting response rules inside each \problem body against the expecteds bound to that id. Here that means entries for problem 2's remaining rods (3) and cubes (3) as well as 33, and entries for problem 3's rounded operands (60 and 30) as well as the estimate 30 -- the modelling steps a concept-models task is graded on.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose problem prints three response slots ('how many ten rods', 'how many ones cubes', 'the number') with a single eval entry: check_layout must exit non-zero. Passes today; after the fix only the three-entry version passes.
improvements.expected_impact: The place-value intermediate values become machine-checked, so a key that mis-states the blocks left but reaches the right difference could no longer ship green.
improvements.risk: Existing verify files need back-filling, and the slot counter must distinguish response rules from decorative rules in figures and headers.

case_summary: Accurate, well-sequenced elementary subtraction: all nine worksheet checks and all six study-guide checks recompute correctly, the four representations build on one another with scaffolding that fades between problems 4 and 5, and the three declared traps compute the wrong value from the wrong method. Two verification defects sit behind the 32/32. Problem 8 demands a written explanation and is recorded as a bare eval, so the sheet ships with the claim that nothing needs manual review -- untrue. And problems 2 and 3 print three and two response slots respectively against one entry each, leaving the rod-and-cube counts and the rounded operands unverified. One wording nit worth noting though not worth a backlog entry: problem 1 asks 'How many blocks are left?' after crossing out 2 rods and 3 cubes, where a literal object count is 6, not 24 -- the following '47 - 23 =' is what disambiguates it.
